source.how: get_computed_styles for the declared values; get_node_info / get_children for the laid-out rects, whose world coordinates are what `gaps` is computed from.

note: The two voices, one case each — which is the point of measuring this component at all. The sender is a padded, rounded box; the receiver is a track with NO inset, no fill and no corner, and the only thing holding it together is the 12px between the answer and its actions row. A spec that covered only the bubble would be measuring the half of this design that looks like a component.

lawsNotDeclared.uniform-inset: The inset is 16 inline and 12 block ON PURPOSE — space-lg against space-md, the same asymmetry Tooltip's chip declares. A bubble padded uniformly at 16 reads as a card; at 12 the text touches the corner's curve. Declaring uniformity here would fail a drawing that is right.
lawsNotDeclared.concentric-radius: The attachment tile carries Thumbnail's own radius-md and sits a full inset inside the bubble's radius-lg. Concentricity is arithmetic on ONE padding, and this box has two — 8 + 12 block against 8 + 16 inline cannot both equal 16, so the law has no single answer to check here.
Nothing in the receiver paints a fill, a border or a corner — that absence IS the design, and an unpainted radius is not a fact about it.

deviations.what: The sheet's text node is 38px (two wrapped lines of the anatomy specimen's own string) and its tile is a flat 48px rectangle; the render's are whatever the mounted string and the mounted tile produce.
deviations.why: The case exists for the 8px between the two rows and the 12/16 inset, both of which hold at any line count. Pinning 38 would pin a sentence rather than a design.

deviations.what: The measured container is the receiver ROOT (data-slot chat-message, data-role receiver), which the sender also matches by slot name — so the render case mounts the receiver alone.
deviations.why: Both voices are one item and share the root slot deliberately: a consumer styling `[data-slot="chat-message"]` means both, and the role is on the same node as a data attribute. The geometry test selects the first match, so the case is written with one message on screen.

deviations.what: The actions row is pinned visible in the render case.
deviations.why: It is opacity-0 until hover or focus, and opacity does not move a rect — but a case that depends on a hover the test never performs is a case whose second child might silently be the wrong element. Pinning it makes the figure the one the sheet drew.
